paths.description: Homepage and primary news discovery template; covers first-load chrome, lead stories, navigation, privacy, network, performance, preferences, and mobile layout.
Finanzas y Mercados listing template representing section and feed pages.
Representative news article and primary reading journey, including crawler/no-JS coverage.
Live dollar/market-data archetype representing data-heavy utility pages.
Federated identity/account entry archetype representing account access.
Deliberately unknown URL used to inspect HTTP/not-found recovery.

findings.summary: The site does not honor the user’s dark-color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually identical to the light design, and the CSS probe found no prefers-color-scheme rule on any representative template.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces, text, controls, and embedded UI through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Long-running motion continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, eight animations remained running, including 15–24 second ticker animations and pulsing elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential ticker and pulse animations in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query and stop auto-advance.

findings.summary: Primary template changes are abrupt on key routes.
findings.evidence: CSS probes found no View Transition support on the homepage or representative article, despite cross-document navigation being a primary interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for article and section navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long pages do not provide scroll-state guidance.
findings.evidence: The article is over 15,800 CSS pixels tall, but the captured template exposes no reading progress or scroll-aware article chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight declarative reading-progress affordance to long articles and keep sticky chrome responsive to scroll state.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures every audited page on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a full-page dimmer and large consent panel before interaction, with an additional Google sign-in prompt on desktop.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking consent wall with a compact, non-obscuring consent control and defer secondary sign-in prompts until user intent.

findings.summary: The blocking consent UI is custom chrome rather than a semantic dialog.
findings.evidence: DOM probes found one large fixed overlay but zero dialog or popover elements; its modal behavior is implemented as nested divs.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a real dialog only if modality is necessary, provide programmatic naming/focus handling, and use declarative close actions.

findings.summary: Competing fixed chrome crowds the news content.
findings.evidence: The first viewport combines a full consent wall, a separate Google sign-in prompt, subscription chrome, ticker, bottom navigation, and a chat control.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate persistent chrome, remove simultaneous prompts, and reserve the first viewport for the lead story and navigation.

findings.summary: Several controls have undersized hit areas.
findings.evidence: Focus probes found 3–4 visible controls below 24px in one dimension, including a 132×15 edition button and 18×22 modal close control.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive boxes to at least 24×24 CSS pixels, preferably 44×44 on touch layouts, without shrinking visible focus.

findings.summary: Unknown URLs silently redirect to the homepage.
findings.evidence: Requesting a deliberately nonexistent URL ended at https://www.cronista.com/ with no 404 heading or recovery explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Return an honest 404 status and a focused not-found page with search, section links, and a route back to the previous context.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is far outside the good range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 17.6s, LCP 26.7s, TBT 300ms, and a 0.49 performance score; a separate trace measured LCP 3.03s under a less-throttled condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content, reduce third-party startup work, and enforce performance budgets using throttled field-like testing.

findings.summary: JavaScript startup consumes substantial main-thread time.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported 4.1s main-thread work and 2.2s JavaScript execution; Clickio, React, and Permutive were leading contributors.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential vendors until consent/interaction, split first-party bundles, and schedule remaining work in short prioritized tasks.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is dominated by a large script and vendor chain.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 109 requests and 3.19MB transferred; 2.24MB was script, and the 568KB first-party default bundle took 2.31s.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce and split the default bundle, preload only true critical assets, and keep async/defer on non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the load.
findings.evidence: HAR measured 58 third-party requests and 1.77MB third-party transfer, including duplicate analytics tags, reCAPTCHA, consent, identity, and advertising scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory vendor value, remove duplicate analytics, and load optional identity, ads, and recaptcha only on paths that need them.

findings.summary: Accessible names and alternatives are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed image-alt and link-name; the image primitive found 2 missing alts on home and 10 on the article, while DOM probes found unlabeled search inputs.
findings.suggestedFix: Give meaningful images useful alt text, decorative images empty alt, every link an accessible name, and every field a programmatic label.

findings.summary: Many text elements fail minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast failed with 201 affected nodes.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground and background design tokens to meet WCAG AA and retest all card, ticker, footer, and consent states.

findings.summary: Heading and focus semantics are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The homepage h1 is empty, article markup contains several empty headings, and focused menu links were observed with outline: none.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove empty headings, give the homepage a meaningful h1, and ensure every interactive element has a visible :focus-visible style.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured a React Internal Server Error, a first-party content API 500, CORS errors, and failed resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the failing content request, handle vendor failures without console noise, and add production error monitoring with actionable ownership.

findings.summary: Image markup and sizing are unsound at scale.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 87/100 homepage images and 28/39 article images without width/height, mostly legacy formats; Lighthouse also found aspect-ratio and low-resolution failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit accurate width/height or aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes, and modern formats from the image component.

findings.summary: Large first-party scripts lack usable source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the valid-source-maps audit for large first-party JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish production source maps to authorized tooling or provide correctly linked hidden source maps for debugging.

findings.summary: Transport protections and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP is only upgrade-insecure-requests; HSTS and nosniff are missing, and all seven observed cookies were flagged, including one non-Secure cookie.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP, HSTS, nosniff, secure cookie defaults, and stricter SameSite values where cross-site use is unnecessary.

findings.summary: The first load exposes users to an extensive tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 32 third-party origins and six known tracker domains; HAR attributed 58 requests and 1.77MB to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential vendors before consent, minimize identifiers and retention, and consolidate analytics into a small first-party-controlled pipeline.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are largely absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no HSTS, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or X-Content-Type-Options, while CSP lacks a source policy and frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Set frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, nosniff and HSTS; expand CSP to explicit script/style/connect sources and nonces.

findings.summary: The app-like news experience has no install manifest or verified offline fallback.
findings.evidence: All templates expose service-worker capability but no manifest link; offline behavior is not presented as a user-facing capability.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a valid web app manifest and a service-worker offline fallback for saved or recently read articles.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling is misleading.
findings.evidence: A nonexistent path redirected to the homepage, and the live homepage also produced a first-party API 500 with no visible recovery state.
findings.suggestedFix: Preserve truthful status codes and provide specific retry, search, and navigation recovery states for failed content.

findings.summary: Consent copy frames tracking acceptance as required for free browsing.
findings.evidence: The blocking panel headline says “Accept cookies to browse for free” although a reject action exists, while consent text describes device identification and 1,719 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Use neutral consent language, equal visual weight and order for accept/reject, and make browsing available without non-essential tracking.

findings.summary: The subscription call to action omits the commitment period.
findings.evidence: Persistent chrome advertises “Suscribite x $999” without a visible billing period or renewal terms in the same decision context.
findings.suggestedFix: Show billing cadence, renewal terms, and cancellation access beside the subscription price before navigation.

findings.summary: Most image assets use legacy formats or lack responsive metadata.
findings.evidence: The homepage image audit found 93 legacy-format images, 87 missing dimensions, 16 missing srcset, and 9 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, emit responsive srcset/sizes and intrinsic dimensions, and right-size every card image.

findings.summary: Background and startup work is disproportionate to a news homepage.
findings.evidence: The load made 109 requests and ran analytics, ads, identity, recaptcha, push, chat, and measurement code before the user engaged.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer optional vendors until consent and intent, batch analytics, and stop background work when the page is hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party transfer exceeds half of the page load.
findings.evidence: Third parties transferred 1.77MB of the 3.19MB total and accounted for 58 requests; scripts represented 2.24MB overall.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors, and lazy-load media and advertising slots near the viewport.
